checks: Codes use eight unambiguous cryptographic characters; rules, profiles, signaling and ICE inputs are bounded
Host creates a short-code room; joining clients exchange a bounded roster, ready status and host-only rules
Twenty-Hz owner poses and ten-Hz host AI/time reach all clients; late join starts the same run and full rooms reject cleanly
Clients cannot change host rules or inject shared-world events; replayed packets and nonfinite player poses are rejected
Host-only game events preserve target IDs; names remain data, and snapshot size/backpressure cannot grow transport queues
Away state removes a remote car from active play; ping, timeout and client departure have bounded cleanup
Host departure ends clients, destroys connections and discards queued starts; cancelled factory completion cannot create a zombie room
Real 36-car and 6-officer world snapshots survive transport validation and apply to matching replicas without local AI advancement
Actual remote cars interpolate wrapped headings and wheel motion, snap teleports, carry damage/lights and expose matching audio/contact poses
limits: Protocol tests use an in-memory PeerJS-compatible transport. They do not prove ICE traversal, signaling availability or real browser WebRTC connectivity.
Remote geometry tests use actual Three.js and createCar without GPU rendering.
Solid player contacts are local kinematic contacts; no rollback or anti-cheat system is asserted.
